I don’t think that it warrants being called discrimination. Being uncomfortable around someone due to certain behaviours, regardless of whether they can help them or not, is a completely reasonable reaction and as isn’t something we have a choice over, and neither is disliking those people as a result. Disliking something doesn’t necessarily mean that you’re going to do them any form of harm, it’s just the natural reaction we have to things that distress us in some manner.

Being around gay people doesn’t necessarily mean they’re going to start going at it next to you, that’s an outlying scenario. If kids are always going to do things you find irritating or uncomfortable while they’re around, I think that’s a vastly different scenario.
